battle.name: 法拉波斯戰爭
battle.brief: 一八三五年十一月秘魯越過南部山界進攻厄瓜多，塔爾基一役厄軍在札魯米拉河谷正面擊潰秘軍，弗洛雷斯負傷退回基多，戰事延至一八四五年。卡面長槍屬已被火槍刺刀取代的舊式兵器，實際決戰靠燧發步槍、刺刀與騎兵長矛。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 交戰的兩方是南美洲的秘魯共和國與厄瓜多共和國，主要戰場在今日厄瓜多南部的洛哈省、埃爾奧羅省以及更北的厄瓜多亞馬遜低地一帶。秘魯一方以巴爾維揚政府為核心，國防由陸軍與海軍分掌：遠征軍由一名陸軍准將以上的將領統一率領，下轄步兵旅、獨立炮兵連與工兵隊，線列步兵營以燧發滑膛槍為制式武器，另有邊境民兵與地方守備隊擔任後方警戒；後勤由軍需署掌理，糧秣、彈藥與炮件多以驢隊、馱馬沿安第斯山東麓的皇家驛道運往洛哈以及往楚斯科方向的倉庫。厄瓜多一方是弗洛雷斯主持的共和國政府，平時倚重基多駐軍與洛哈邊境部隊，兵員補充靠民兵與城鎮自願者，新格拉納達與委內瑞拉提供的志願兵與軍械屬外來援助；海權方面只有瓜亞基爾的數艘小型武裝船與走私船可用，負責封鎖、偵察與沿岸運輸。兩邊的指揮系統都帶著鮮明的西班牙殖民遺制：總統兼最高統帥直接下達作戰命令，參謀部擬定行軍與部署，軍需與工程兵處理道路、渡河與糧秣徵發，傳令多靠人力騎馬與信鴿，山地環境令任何一紙計畫都難以落實到連隊。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Republic of Peru and the Republic of Ecuador in South America, and the principal theatre lay across what are now the Ecuadorian provinces of Loja and El Oro and the Ecuadorian Amazon lowlands further north. On the Peruvian side the government of José Ballivián was the political centre, with the army and the navy each holding part of national defence: the expeditionary force was led by a general of at least divisional rank and organised into infantry brigades, separate batteries and an engineer detachment, with line infantry battalions armed with flintlock muskets, while frontier militias and local garrisons provided rear-area security. Logistics were the responsibility of the intendants, and food, powder and ammunition were moved by mule and pack-horse trains along the royal road on the eastern slopes of the Andes towards the depots at Loja and towards the stores in the direction of Cusco. On the Ecuadorian side stood the republican government of Juan José Flores, relying for the most part on the Quito garrison and the frontier troops of Loja, with numbers supplemented by militias and town volunteers, while volunteers and stores supplied from New Granada and Venezuela counted as outside assistance; at sea it had only a handful of small armed vessels and privateers out of Guayaquil, used for blockade work, reconnaissance and coastal transport. Both command systems carried the stamp of the Spanish colonial inheritance: the president acted as supreme commander and issued operational orders directly, a general staff drew up the marches and deployments, the intendants and the engineers handled roads, river crossings and the requisition of food, and messages travelled by mounted messenger and by carrier pigeon, since the mountain country made it very hard to make any written plan reach the company.
people: 關鍵人物集中在厄瓜多一方。總統胡安·何塞·弗洛雷斯是這場衝突的象徵；他出身陸軍，在大哥倫比亞邦聯解體前後於基多推動「厄瓜多回應」運動，把厄瓜多從邦聯中分出並自任領袖，其後成為共和國的首任元首。他在政敵與外人嘴裡有「法老」的綽號，「法拉波斯」一名通常被認為正是敵人對他和他手下那批人的諷稱。一八三五年六月，厄瓜多南部爆發「至尊派」起義，由文森特·羅卡富埃特與何塞·路易斯·皮科率領，起義兵在蒂克桑一役被弗洛雷斯擊潰，兩人出逃，羅卡富埃特其後流亡並在四十年代回國奪取總統位；同年十一月秘軍越境時，弗洛雷斯剛剛騰出手來，據說正是這場平亂讓他敢於在南部用兵。塔爾基一役中弗洛雷斯在前線督戰並在交鋒中受傷，被抬回基多，隨後靠城防與政治手腕重整軍隊。秘魯方面，巴爾維揚以總統身分拍板出兵，把一場邊界糾紛升級為戰爭；一八三七年後由多明戈·涅托接任，於一八三八年再舉遠征。新格拉納達總統何塞·伊拉里奧·洛佩斯與委內瑞拉方面也提供了有限的支援與外交聲援。英國與法國的軍艦則在瓜亞基爾外海活動，藉封鎖港口向秘魯施壓，因而與厄瓜多、海軍及後來扣押英法船隻的衝突牽連在一起。
peopleEn: The key figures are concentrated on the Ecuadorian side. The president, Juan José Flores, is the very symbol of the conflict. He came out of the army, and as the great Colombian federation broke up he drove the 'Replica del Ecuador' movement in Quito, detached Ecuador from the federation and made himself its leader, later becoming the first head of the republic. His opponents and foreigners called him 'the Pharaoh', and the name 'Farapos' is generally taken to be the derisive label his enemies gave to him and to the men who fought under him. In June 1835 the 'Supremes' revolt broke out in the south of Ecuador under Vicente Rocafuerte and José Luis Pico; the insurgents were beaten at Tixán by Flores, the two leaders fled, and Rocafuerte later returned from exile and took the presidency in the 1840s. When Peruvian troops crossed the border in November of the same year, Flores had only just freed his hands, and the suppression of the revolt is said to be what allowed him to commit forces in the south. At Tarqui he personally supervised the fighting, was wounded in the engagement and was carried back to Quito, where he rebuilt his army by a combination of the city defences and political manoeuvring. On the Peruvian side, Ballivián, in his capacity as president, authorised the campaign and raised a boundary dispute to the level of a war; he was succeeded by Domingo Nieto, who renewed the invasion in 1838. President José Hilario López of New Granada and the Venezuelan government gave limited support and diplomatic backing. British and French warships also operated off Guayaquil, pressing Peru by blockade and so becoming entangled with the Ecuadorian navy and with later seizures of British and French shipping.
kits: 卡面那支一六〇〇年的西班牙長槍，在一八三五年早已不是野戰主力。十六、十七世紀的方陣步兵靠長槍在前排頂住騎兵衝擊，後排火槍隊再從槍林後面射擊；這套組合在歐洲與密西西比一帶退場之後，被火槍加刺刀取代，長槍只留作儀仗、守備與新兵的操練教具，連它的名號都漸漸變成一種榮譽的裝飾。厄瓜多與秘魯的野戰部隊這時早已不用長槍方陣：線列步兵一律配發燧發滑膛槍，膛口口徑約莫零點六九英吋上下，配刺刀；部分營制表上仍留有「持矛兵」的名號，實際裝備早已改為火槍。兩國軍隊中真正還大量使用矛的地方是騎兵，安第斯與山地的輕騎兵仍以長矛配馬槍作戰，衝鋒時靠矛尖與馬匹的衝力撕開步兵隊形。炮兵方面，雙方有四磅與六磅山炮以及十二磅野炮，數量不多，靠驢隊拆件運送，遇山道狹窄便要分解由人力搬運，砲管與砲架的規格也因路而異。餘下的裝備多是帆布帳篷、驢鞍、火藥桶、備用槍管與修槍工具，軍中沒有制式地圖，嚮導多為當地獵戶與牧人，路線選擇與糧秣徵發極依賴這些人。
kitsEn: The Spanish pike of 1600 on the card face was long past being a field weapon by 1835. In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries pike blocks met the charge of cavalry in front while musketeers fired from behind the hedge of pikes; once that combination had been retired in Europe and around the Mississippi, it was replaced by musket and bayonet, and the pike survived only as ceremonial dress, garrison duty and a drill implement for new recruits, its name itself becoming a mark of honour. The field armies of both Ecuador and Peru had long since abandoned the pike square: line infantry were uniformly issued flintlock muskets of roughly .69 inch calibre together with bayonets, and although the tables of organisation in some units still kept the title of pikemen, the actual equipment was already the musket. The one place where the lance was still used in bulk was the cavalry, where light horsemen on the Andean heights fought with lance and carbine, breaking infantry formations with the point of the lance and the weight of the horse. On the artillery side the two sides fielded four- and six-pound mountain guns and twelve-pound field pieces, few in number, carried in pieces on mule trains and broken down for hand-lifting where the mountain track was too narrow, with barrel and carriage dimensions varying according to the road. Everything else in the train was canvas, pack saddles, powder barrels, spare barrels and armourer's tools; the armies had no standard maps, guides were drawn from local hunters and herdsmen, and the choice of route and the collection of food depended on them almost entirely.
tactics: 秘魯遠征軍的戰術是一條典型的高地入侵線：軍隊沿安第斯山東麓與海岸山脈之間的縱谷行進，靠洛哈以西的邊境小道越過山界，企圖先取洛哈城與札魯米拉河谷的「口門」，再向基多方向壓進；厄瓜多軍不願在縱谷中與其纏鬥，於是把主力集結在洛哈以北的山口一帶，用地形把秘軍擠進狹窄的札魯米拉河谷。塔爾基一役的關鍵是地形而非火力：厄瓜多軍先以少量前哨與散兵佔住道路兩側的高地，再讓主力在谷口展開，秘軍進入谷地之後既無法展開兵員，也無法迂迴側面，只能在狹窄正面硬攻；步兵在百餘步到兩百步內完成射擊，接著以刺刀接戰，秘軍中央被突破之後全線退向洛哈，厄軍一路追擊到城郊。此後形勢反覆：秘軍重新集結兵力正面推進，同時派部隊封鎖厄瓜多南部城鎮，切斷洛哈的糧道；厄瓜多則以縱深防守配合側翼襲擊，盡量不讓秘軍在城鎮中打巷戰。一八三七與一八三八至三九年的幾役，雙方都重複同一套模式，先奪山口、斷糧道、再攻城，每一次的勝負都取決於誰先控制洛哈通往基多的山間路徑。一八四一至四二年的交火則轉入亞馬遜低地，部隊沿河溯流而上，叢林、沼澤與黃熱病使任何列陣都失去意義，後方甚至在戰鬥尚未結束之前就已耗盡。
tacticsEn: The Peruvian expedition followed a classic highland invasion: the columns marched along the valleys between the eastern slopes of the Andes and the coastal range, crossed the frontier by the tracks west of Loja, and aimed to seize the town of Loja and the Portón above the Zarumilla valley before pressing on towards Quito. The Ecuadorians declined to give battle in the open valleys and instead massed their main force north of Loja, using the ground to squeeze the Peruvians into the narrow bed of the Zarumilla. The decisive element at Tarqui was therefore the terrain rather than firepower: a few outposts and skirmishers were posted on the heights flanking the road, the main body deployed at the mouth of the valley, and once the Peruvians had entered they could neither deploy their numbers nor turn their flank, so they could only attack frontally in a narrow column. The infantry fired at a range of a hundred to two hundred paces and then closed with the bayonet; the centre of the Peruvian line gave way and the whole formation fell back towards Loja with the Ecuadorians pursuing to the outskirts of the town. Afterwards the pattern repeated: the Peruvians massed again for a frontal advance while detachments blocked the southern towns of Ecuador and cut the food road to Loja; the Ecuadorians answered with a defence in depth combined with attacks on the flanks, doing what they could to keep the fighting out of the streets of the towns. In the campaigns of 1837 and 1838 to 1839 both sides repeated the same sequence, taking a mountain pass, cutting the supply line, and then attacking a town, and the outcome of each depended on who seized the mountain road from Loja to Quito first. The fighting of 1841 to 1842 shifted into the Amazon lowlands, where the troops moved upriver; jungle, swamp and yellow fever robbed any formation of meaning, and the rear services were exhausted before the shooting had finished.
data: 時間上有幾個對得上的點。一八三五年十一月秘軍越境，十二月五日的塔爾基一役厄瓜多軍即取得全勝，秘軍主力退回安第斯山東麓；其後秘方增兵再入，一度據有洛哈與埃爾奧羅一帶，翌年八月二日《馬帕辛格條約》簽訂，第一次高潮才告結束。之後一八三七年、一八三八至三九年、一八四一至四二年各有新一輪交火，到一八四五年最後一次邊界衝突之後，這一連串戰事方告一段落。兵力各家記錄相差頗大，一般認為一八三五年十一月的秘軍遠征部隊在兩三千人上下，厄瓜多軍連民兵與外來志願兵約四五千人；塔爾基一役秘軍被俘與陣亡者以數百計，厄軍亦有相當數量的傷亡。距離與地勢同樣重要：戰場在洛哈以北、通往馬查拉的老路上，與洛哈城相距約莫數十公里的山路，谷地寬度不過數百步；基多到洛哈的山路長達數百公里，步兵行軍要走上數日，全程補給全靠驢隊。武器數據上，燧發滑膛槍每兵只攜帶有限火藥與紙包彈藥，單兵射擊速度緩慢；炮兵僅數十門，砲彈一旦用罄便無從補充。若看非戰鬥減員，一八四一至四二年在亞馬遜低地的部隊因黃熱病與瘧疾損失慘重，許多士兵根本沒有走到前線。上述數字史載互有出入，較保守的說法是這樣，諸說並存之處不宜當作定論。
dataEn: There are several points that can be fixed in time. Peruvian troops crossed the border in November 1835, and on 5 December the Ecuadorians won the whole battle of Tarqui, the main Peruvian body falling back onto the eastern slopes of the Andes; Peru then reinforced and entered again, for a time holding Loja and El Oro, and only with the signing of the Treaty of Mapasingue on 2 August of the following year did the first phase come to an end. After that came fresh rounds of fighting in 1837, in 1838 to 1839 and in 1841 to 1842, and only after the last border clash of 1845 did the whole series of wars come to an end. The numbers of men differ widely between the sources; the Peruvian expeditionary force in November 1835 is generally put at two or three thousand, while the Ecuadorian army, counting militia and foreign volunteers, is given at four or five thousand. At Tarqui the Peruvian dead and prisoners ran to several hundreds, and the Ecuadorians also suffered considerable casualties. Distance and ground matter just as much: the battlefield lay north of Loja on the old road to Machala, some tens of kilometres of mountain road from the town, and the valley itself was no more than a few hundred paces wide. The mountain road from Quito to Loja runs for several hundred kilometres, infantry needed several days to cover it, and the whole of the supply depended on mule trains. On the materiel side each flintlock musket carried only a limited quantity of powder and paper cartridges, the rate of individual fire was slow, and there were only some dozens of guns, so that once the shot was spent there was no way to replace it. On non-combat losses, the troops in the Amazon lowlands in 1841 to 1842 were devastated by yellow fever and malaria, and many of the men never reached the front line at all. These figures vary from source to source; the account above is the more conservative one, and where the records disagree none of them should be taken as settled.
cause: 起火點是邊界糾紛，而邊界糾紛又來自大哥倫比亞邦聯解體後留下的空白。一八三〇年委內瑞拉與新格拉納達先後退出邦聯，厄瓜多也以「厄瓜多回應」運動取得獨立，但三國在北部亞馬遜河上游的界線從未劃定：秘魯主張對馬亞斯、查米庫羅與耶貝羅斯一帶的宗主權，厄瓜多則以實際佔領與傳教站作為佔有依據，雙方各執一詞。海邊一端的洛哈與埃爾奧羅同樣懸而未決，哥倫比亞時期的實際控制線與秘魯堅持的歷史疆界並不一致，一八三一年兩國簽過協議又未見落實，秘魯軍方遂把「未劃界」視為可以動手的理由。第二個藉口是庇護流亡者：厄瓜多境內收留了秘魯的流亡軍人與反對派，秘魯政府把這視為干涉內政。再加上厄瓜多一八三五年六月爆發的「至尊派」起義，首都與南部邊區同時吃緊，主力被牽制的厄瓜多看來無力應戰，秘魯估計時機成熟，遂在十一月出兵。整件事還有一層背景：玻利瓦爾已死，厄瓜多與秘魯是西屬南美最後兩個仍然獨立的共和國，這場戰爭因此也帶著國家認同與建軍路徑之爭的味道。
causeEn: The flashpoint was a boundary dispute, and the boundary dispute in turn grew out of the blank spaces left by the dissolution of the great Colombian federation. In 1830 Venezuela and New Granada left the federation in turn, and Ecuador also won its independence through the 'Replica del Ecuador', but the line between the three countries in the upper Amazon was never drawn: Peru claimed sovereignty over Maynas, Chamicuro and the country of Yeboros, while Ecuador rested its title on actual occupation and on mission stations, and each side held fast to its own version. On the seaward end, Loja and El Oro were equally unsettled, because the line actually held during the Colombian years did not match the historical frontier Peru insisted upon; the two countries had signed an agreement in 1831 and it had not been carried out, and the Peruvian military therefore came to treat an undrawn frontier as a licence to use force. A second pretext was the sheltering of exiles: Ecuador was giving refuge to Peruvian soldiers and opposition men in exile, and the government in Lima read that as interference in its internal affairs. Add to that the 'Supremes' revolt that broke out in Ecuador in June 1835, which tied down the capital and the southern border districts at once; with the Ecuadorian army evidently unable to answer, and Peru judging the moment favourable, an invasion was ordered in November. Behind it all lay a wider background: Bolivar was dead, and Ecuador and Peru were the last two republics still standing in Spanish South America, so the war also carried a flavour of national identity and of rival claims to how a state should be armed.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果，是把厄瓜多與秘魯之間的邊界大致固定下來，也把兩國之間最難纏的一筆賬推到下一次。一八三六年之後，厄瓜多放棄對亞馬遜上游的主張，秘魯則放棄洛哈與埃爾奧羅，換來的現狀維持了二十餘年，卻沒有真正解決亞馬遜通道的歸屬；一八五七至五八年的戰爭與一八九一年的軍事佔領都源出此處，十九世紀末到二十世紀初的圭亞那與委內瑞拉邊界危機也與同一條線相連。就厄瓜多內部而言，一八三五年的「至尊派」平亂讓弗洛雷斯的中央集權路線得到鞏固，卻同時把最偏遠的南部省份推向不滿，於是有了「至尊派」捲土重來與一八三八年的內戰；一八四四年弗洛雷斯再度當選並被冠以「法老」之名，一八四五年三月卻被軍人與文人聯手推翻，羅卡富埃特接位，「法拉波斯」的名號也隨着這批人馬的潰散而淡出史冊。軍事技術上，這是西屬南美獨立之後的一場樣板戰：野戰由燧發滑膛槍加刺刀主導，沒有長槍方陣，也沒有火槍輪射的密集火力，個人勇武與地形比裝備更能左右勝負，這一點在後來南美洲其他衝突中重複出現。
impactEn: The outcome of the war was to fix the border between Ecuador and Peru more or less as it stands, and to push the most intractable of their mutual claims on to a later round. After 1836 Ecuador gave up its claim to the upper Amazon while Peru abandoned Loja and El Oro; the status quo so obtained lasted for more than twenty years, yet it never truly settled who owned the Amazonian approaches, for the war of 1857 to 1858 and the military occupation of 1891 both grew out of it, and the boundary crises between British Guiana and Venezuela at the end of the nineteenth century and the beginning of the twentieth were joined to the same thread. Within Ecuador, the suppression of the 'Supremes' in 1835 confirmed the centralising line of Flores, but at the same time it drove the most remote southern provinces into opposition, and the stage was set both for the 'Supremes' to rise again and for the civil war of 1838. In 1844 Flores was returned to the presidency and once more given the name of Pharaoh; in March 1845 he was overthrown by a combination of soldiers and intellectuals, Rocafuerte succeeded him, and the name of the 'Farapos' faded from history along with the rout of the men who bore it. On the military side this was a model war for Spanish South America after independence: field combat was led by flintlock musket and bayonet, with no pike square and no dense volley fire, and individual bravery and the ground counted for more than the quality of the equipment, a pattern that was to repeat in later South American conflicts.
result: 結果可以分幾層看。戰術層面，一八三五年十二月五日塔爾基一役是全場的轉折：秘軍在狹窄的札魯米拉河谷被厄瓜多軍正面擊潰，弗洛雷斯在前線受傷退回基多，秘軍退回安第斯山東麓，此後再未能在厄瓜多南部站穩。外交層面，一八三六年八月二日的《馬帕辛格條約》確定洛哈與埃爾奧羅歸厄瓜多，馬亞斯與查米庫羅歸秘魯，雙方回到大致以邦聯時期界線為基礎的現狀；一八三七、一八三八至三九、一八四一至四二年又各自爆發新一輪交火，每次都因糧秣與援兵不濟而不了了之，最後一輪邊界衝突延續到一八四五年。政治層面，戰爭沒有改變兩國的基本疆界，卻加速了弗洛雷斯的軍人政權，也在其對手心中種下反感，一八四五年他被推翻時，原先跟隨他的那批人便帶著「法拉波斯」的稱號退場。總的來說，這是一場為邊界而打、卻沒有靠戰爭解決邊界問題的戰爭；真正被它改變的，是安第斯山兩側兩個共和國之間的邊界想像，以及此後一百年亞馬遜爭端的走向。
resultEn: The result can be read at several levels. On the tactical level, the battle of Tarqui on 5 December 1835 was the turning point of the whole affair: the Peruvian army was broken frontally in the narrow valley of the Zarumilla, Flores was wounded at the front and fell back to Quito, the Peruvians withdrew onto the eastern slopes of the Andes, and they were never afterwards able to establish themselves again in southern Ecuador. On the diplomatic level, the Treaty of Mapasingue of 2 August 1836 settled Loja and El Oro to Ecuador and Maynas and Chamicuro to Peru, and the two sides returned to a status quo based more or less on the frontier lines of the federation era; new rounds of fighting broke out in 1837, in 1838 to 1839 and in 1841 to 1842, each of them fizzling out for want of food and reinforcements, and the last of the border clashes ran on into 1845. On the political level the war changed neither country's essential frontiers, but it hastened the coming of Flores's military government and sowed resentment among his opponents, and when he was overthrown in 1845 the men who had followed him left the stage still carrying the name of the 'Farapos'. In sum this was a war fought for a frontier that did not settle the frontier question by force; what it really changed was the idea each of the two Andean republics entertained of its own border, and the direction the Amazon dispute would take over the following century.
